summary: Michael L. Walter specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry Moses and held posts as a Research Fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and Special Languages Cataloger at Indiana University (attested 2020).
Michael M. Broido specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge, taught Shenpen Hookham, and held a post at the University of Oxford.
Michael Oppitz (born 1942) works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987–1988) and the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).

Michael Puett (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Anthony C. Yu (~1987–1994) and was appointed John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Humanities at Harvard University (~1994).

Michael Pye (born 1939) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under Maurice Wiles and held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1970–1978) and Lancaster University (~1991–1995), where he served as Professor.

Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2007) supervised by Robert M. Gimello, also studying at Kyoto University (2009). He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (~2005–2017) and Heidelberg University (~2018).
Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from the University of Bristol and pursued PhD candidacy at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, serving as Redaktor des Wörterbuchs (attested 1981), in 1992, and as Mitarbeiter (attested 2008).

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019).

Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology who earned an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. He has held posts at the Max Planck Institute, Leipzig University, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.

Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991). He has held a post as a fellow at the University of Hamburg.
Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1838–1847) and later held a post there (~1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister (born 1942) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1964–1967) and Harvard University (~1968–1974), and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1976–2020).

Michael Witzel (born 1943) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Paul Thieme (~1967–1971) and held posts as Director of the Nepal Research Centre (~1972–1977), Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978–1986), and Chair of Sanskrit at Harvard University (1987).

Michael Zimmermann (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and others. His posts include the Nepal Research Centre (2002), Stanford University (2003), and University of Hamburg Director (attested 2009–2015).

Michael von Brück (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Regensburg (~1988–1991) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1991–2015).

Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Peter Schwieger, and studied under Rechungpa and traditional teacher Jigme Namgyal.

Michaela Mross is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (-2014). She held posts at the University of Göttingen, UC Berkeley, and Stanford University (attested 2017).

Michel Bréal (1832–1915) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at École Normale Supérieure, and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as Professor at Collège de France (1866–1905) and Director at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).

Michel Clasquin (born 1960) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of South Africa, where he completed degrees in 1991, 1993, and a doctoral thesis in 1999, and held a post there in 1990.
